biography.html: H. Gary Morse developed The Villages, Florida's extensive retirement community, from a mobile-home business established by his father, Harold Schwartz. Raised in Michigan, he moved south in 1983 to take charge of the project. He expanded its housing and amenities while retaining an ownership interest as his children assumed senior responsibilities.

long_biography.html:
When residents proposed a woodworking club, H. Gary Morse expanded their plan, found a site and equipped a building for them. The idea had begun with neighbours making Christmas toys in their garages. His support gave the volunteer founders a shared workshop instead of moving production between separate homes.

He also sought a university partner to study retirement health. In 2011, The Villages joined the University of South Florida in a community health study, with plans for focus groups and baseline research. The collaboration brought together public-health, medical and information-technology expertise to explore how residents could maintain their health as they aged.
